penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: SharePoint migration is fundamentally a hands-on project: source/destination mapping, permissions audit, test migrations, cutover — all require direct human involvement per engagement.

penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: Migration projects require scoping calls, stakeholder alignment, and sign-off before execution. No self-serve path exists for high-stakes enterprise data migration.

penalties_applied.name: high_touch_support
penalties_applied.reason: Post-migration validation and issue resolution (missing permissions, broken links) require ongoing human judgment per client.

rationale: IT admins and M365 consultants are real buyers with real budget — ShareGate and Metalogix prove willingness to pay at $300–$500+ per migration. However, the service itself is inherently a hands-on, project-based engagement: every migration requires human scoping, execution oversight, and post-migration validation. Operational autonomy is near zero (score 2). This is a consultancy service dressed as a product, and no amount of Claude automation changes the need for per-customer human project management. Penalties drop total to 2.0.
solution_plan: Not viable for this factory. SharePoint-to-SharePoint migration is a professional services engagement, not a repeatable automated product — the buyer pays for human expertise, not a script. Tools like ShareGate already automate the mechanical parts; what remains is judgment-intensive project work. A solo non-technical operator cannot build a competing migration tool, and offering migration as a service would require Youval's full hands-on involvement per client. Drop this path.
notes: Fails operational_autonomy_min (2 < 7) and buildability_with_ai_min (3 < 6). The market is proven but the delivery model is fundamentally incompatible with autonomous operation.
